exposure: Type of cesarean hysterectomy (elective vs. emergency)
cohort: 45 patients who underwent cesarean hysterectomy (26.7% elective, 73.3% emergency) at two centers in India.
finding: Emergency cesarean hysterectomies are associated with significantly higher rates of adverse maternal outcomes and adverse neonatal outcomes (stillbirth, poor APGAR score) compared to elective cesarean hysterectomies.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean hysterectomies, a specific mode of birth, led to significantly worse maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to elective procedures.
